commenti.body: Why is this sub a lot less active than it was a year ago? I just watched the first 5 episodes of Alfonso Cuarón's Disclaimer and came here looking for some discussion and found nothing. I am really surprised at the lack of enthusiasm for Cuarón's first project since Roma. Personally, I think it is fantastic, but I feel like there is no reason it couldn't have been a movie.

Just watched the last hour of House Of Gucci on TV. Someone tell me - how in the name of all things sane could so many A-list actors imagine is was a good idea to make a film about Italian people and speak English with an Italian accent? Jared Leto sounds like Super Mario. Did no-one have doubts? Al Pacino for crying out loud?! How did this madness happen??

Because A-list actors never get punished for doing bad work. They’re still going to get work, they’re still going to get paid, they’re still going to be fawned over. I’ve been on film sets where the star has their head buried in their phone as they’re counting down to shoot. Any other job, you’d be fired or not hired again for this kind of stuff. But stars can get away with this kind of stuff because the industry is controlled by a very small group of people. And because audiences don’t have high enough standards for acting.
